items.title: Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Search teams have recovered 1010 bodies, with around 4000 people still unaccounted for. More than 11800 people have been rescued so far, including hundreds of foreign nationals.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Foreign nationals — missing, rescued, or contacted (NDRRMA, 1 Sep)
items.summary: Lists with details on foreign nationals after the Bhote Koshi flood in Rasuwa are with the Department of Tourism. A final situation update covers events through August 30.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — X post (1 September 2026)

items.title: Embassy of India — identification of mortal remains (1 Sep 2026)
items.summary: The Indian embassy has put out guidance for families trying to identify remains after the Nepal floods. Relatives can check photos on the police disaster portal or email for DNA matching and contact the helplines listed.
items.citation: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — Press Release (1 September 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescuers have brought out over 10,000 people from the flooded areas, including more than 323 foreigners. So far 903 bodies have been recovered, while about 4,200 people remain unaccounted for and 590 foreign nationals from 39 countries are still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Families of people missing in the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi floods can help identify recovered bodies by giving DNA samples. Relatives in Nepal can bring a fresh blood sample and two photos to the Nepal Police Hospital lab in Maharajgunj or the nearest district police office, while those abroad can send results from an authorised lab.
items.citation: Nepal Police HQ — Information on DNA Profiling for unidentified Dead Bodies (31 Aug)

items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: Water levels in the Bhotekoshi River rose again on Sunday. People in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas should stay careful.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)
items.summary: Flash floods hit the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August. Rescue teams have recovered 734 bodies so far, while 2,498 people remain missing and over 8,186 have been brought to safety.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: The floods hit the Bhote Koshi River on August 26, and rescue teams have recovered 626 bodies so far while about 2400 people are still missing. Over 4450 people have been brought out safely, including 187 foreign nationals, with teams still working in the affected districts.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August, with 538 bodies recovered and hundreds of locals and tourists still missing. Rescue teams are searching the area and providing help to those affected.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue teams and helicopters have reached the mudslide area at Gyirong Port after it hit Wednesday morning. Three people have been killed, 558 remain missing, and two villagers have been rescued so far.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure. So far 359 bodies have been recovered and 596 people from 33 countries remain missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary: Nepal's foreign ministry has opened a help line for families of foreign nationals missing or affected in the Rasuwa floods. Call or message +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 between 7am and 10pm.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: India's foreign ministry has set up a 24-hour control room in Delhi for the Nepal floods. Families can reach the room or the Indian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing through the listed phone and WhatsApp numbers.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal this morning, killing people and damaging homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure. So far 72 bodies have been recovered and 403 people are reported missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026

items.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — assistance for Indian nationals
items.summary: The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is working with Nepalese authorities on search, rescue, and identification after the floods. Indian families can email eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or message the WhatsApp helplines +977-9851316807, +977-9709107500, and +977-9810326117, or reach the Delhi control room at +91-11-23088718 or +91-11-23088719.
